title: Compare Department Average Salary vs Company Average
prompt: Compare each department's average salary against the company-wide average salary. Return department_name, department_avg_salary, company_avg_salary, and comparison_result. The comparison_result should be 'higher', 'lower', or 'same'.
expected_query: WITH department_averages AS (SELECT d.department_name, AVG(e.salary) AS department_avg_salary FROM employees e INNER JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.department_id GROUP BY d.department_name), company_average AS (SELECT AVG(salary) AS company_avg_salary FROM employees) SELECT da.department_name, da.department_avg_salary, ca.company_avg_salary, CASE WHEN da.department_avg_salary > ca.company_avg_salary THEN 'higher' WHEN da.department_avg_salary < ca.company_avg_salary THEN 'lower' ELSE 'same' END AS comparison_result FROM department_averages da CROSS JOIN company_average ca;
explanation: The solution first calculates one average salary per department, then calculates the company-wide average once. CROSS JOIN makes that one company average available beside every department row. CASE WHEN turns the comparison into a readable label.
hints: Create one CTE for department averages.
Create another CTE for the company average.
Use CASE WHEN to compare department_avg_salary with company_avg_salary.
The company average CTE has one row, so CROSS JOIN is a simple way to attach it to each department.
common_mistakes: Grouping by employee instead of department.
Forgetting to join departments before selecting department_name.
Comparing each employee salary instead of each department average.
Using WHERE for aggregate filtering when the comparison belongs in SELECT.
